stories.title: ICE agent charged with lying about shooting Venezuelan man during crackdown
stories.summary: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent has been charged with lying about the non-fatal shooting of a Venezuelan migrant in the state of Minnesota. Christian Castro, who is not yet in custody, faces a six-count federal indictment relating to shooting on 14 January, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS. The Department of Homeland Security initially said he fired in self-defence after being attacked by three Venezuelan illegal migrants with a shovel and broom handle. Minnesota investigators allege Castro fired through a closed door, shooting the man in the leg. It is rare for the current justice department to accuse a federal agent of breaking the law on the job. What is ICE and what powers do its agents have to use force? In Minnesota, Castro faces separate charges of assault and false reporting of a crime related to the shooting. Castro was one of thousands of federal immigration officers deployed to the Midwestern state during Operation Metro Surge, which sparked fierce protests and resulted in the deaths of two US citizens at the hands of agents during confrontations. Alfredo Alejandro Aljorna and Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, who was shot in the leg and survived, were originally charged with forcibly assaulting, resisting or impeding federal officers. After surveillance video raised questions about the agents' version of events, federal prosecutors investigated them. In February, ICE said two immigration agents might have made "untruthful statements" about the shooting. They were placed on administrative leave.

stories.title: Putin to hold meeting of Pobeda organizing committee
stories.summary: President of the Russian Academy of Sciences Gennady Krasnikov will present a report detailing the review process for applications of Hero City title candidates
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 4.
Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold a meeting of the Pobeda (Victory) Organizing Committee via videoconference on September 4.

According to the Kremlin press service, President of the Russian Academy of Sciences Gennady Krasnikov will present a report detailing the review process for applications of Hero City title candidates.

Reports will also be delivered by First Deputy Chairman of the Federation Council and Secretary of the General Council of the United Russia party Vladimir Yakushev, Primorye Region Governor and Chairman of the State Council Commission on Tourism Oleg Kozhemyako, and Executive Secretary of the Search Movement of Russia Elena Tsunayeva.

stories.title: Gwangju Biennale ponders theme of change through works by 43 teams
stories.summary: SEOUL, Sept. 4 (Yonhap) -- The 16th Gwangju Biennale will launch this weekend in...
article_sentences: The 16th Gwangju Biennale will launch this weekend in the southwestern city of Gwangju, with 43 teams from South Korea and abroad presenting works themed on transformation as a continuous process.
This year's event will begin with an opening ceremony Friday evening and officially kick off its 72-day run from Saturday through Nov. 5, according to the Gwangju Biennale Foundation.

Inspired by Rainer Maria Rilke's 1908 poem "Archaic Torso of Apollo," that concludes with the final line "You must change your life," the exhibition brings together works that explore how new capacities and forms of life emerge through change and artistic practice.

At a press conference held in March, artistic director Ho Tzu Nyen remarked how "the Biennale explores change as an artistic method, through which art thinkers, art dreamers and art lovers alike experiment with new forms of life, creativity, power and relationship."

To allow viewers to fully immerse themselves in the featured works, this year's Biennale scaled down the numbers of works on display but gathered them into one venue rather than spreading them across the city.
Featured artists include Mona Benyamin, Angela Goh, Daisuke Kosugi, Kim Sun-ik and James T.

Among notable participants is Volcanoes of Jeju, or Jeju Stone Park, which showcases the volcanic stones from the southern resort island of Jeju, engraved with the explosive eruption of volcanoes and the thousands of years that follow.
Meanwhile, the Biennale's Pavilion Project, which was introduced in 2018 to foster artistic exchange among artists and institutions, was set to feature 16 countries and 11 institutions.

But the plan has faltered amid a controversy over the use of the name Taiwan Pavilion, which prompted participating Chinese artists to hold a press conference saying they will withdraw from the exhibition in protest.
